macro_context.market_sentiment: Mixed-to-bullish: S&P 500 slipped 0.38% to 7,337 on May 7 after Iran ceasefire breakdown, but prior week saw the Nasdaq, S&P 500, and Russell 2000 all hit new record highs driven by AI-sector strength. Market remains resilient despite geopolitical headwinds.
macro_context.fed_outlook: Fed held rates at 3.50-3.75% at the April 29 meeting in an 8-4 split vote — the most dissent since 1992. Fed noted inflation elevated partly due to global energy prices. Consensus expects rates to hold in the 3.25-3.75% range through end of 2026; no near-term cuts expected.
macro_context.geopolitical: Ongoing Iran war is the dominant risk: ceasefire violations reported May 7, oil prices volatile, Strait of Hormuz closure threatens a major energy supply shock. IMF flagged the conflict as the key downside risk to global growth (3.1% forecast) with headline inflation at 4.4%. Markets so far resilient, buoyed by AI momentum.
key_events: Iran ceasefire status — further breakdowns could spike oil and pressure consumer sentiment
Fed next meeting — hold likely but dissent signals policy uncertainty
Q2 earnings season ongoing — broad beats so far supporting equities
Paramount/WBD merger integration — reshapes competitive media landscape

ticker_news.headline: Disney Q2 FY2026 earnings beat: revenue $25.17B (+7% YoY) and EPS $1.57 both topped estimates; streaming income surged 88% to $582M
DIS stock jumped ~7-8% post-earnings, hitting a three-month high; three Wall Street firms raised price targets after 'Q2 Crusher'
New CEO Josh D'Amaro's first earnings call: guided full-year EPS growth ~12% and raised share buyback target to at least $8B for FY2026
ticker_news.source: Walt Disney Company IR / Motley Fool transcript — 2026-05-06

ticker_news.headline: Domestic U.S. park attendance declined 1% YoY in Q2, attributed to fewer international travelers; global attendance up 2%
Raymond James upgraded DIS to Outperform on April 1 with $115 price target, citing attractive valuation after Q1 pullback

analyst_consensus.recent_changes: Post-Q2 earnings (May 6-7): at least three firms raised price targets. Raymond James upgraded to Outperform ($115 target) on April 1. Overall 26 Buy / 4 Hold / 1 Sell out of 42 analysts. Median target ~$131; range $77.77 to $168.00. Avg target ~$132-134 depending on source. Stock trading ~$107-115 range pre/post earnings, suggesting ~15-25% upside to consensus.

competitor_activity: Paramount Skydance acquired Warner Bros. Discovery at $111B (Netflix withdrew its bid), creating a new media giant that will compete more directly with Disney in film and streaming. Comcast spun off CNBC/MSNBC/E! into 'Versant Media Group,' narrowing its streaming focus. Netflix faces growing competition from YouTube on TV screens. Disney's streaming profitability (+88% income to $582M) positions it as one of the strongest legacy media streamers, ahead of Peacock (still narrowing losses) and the newly formed Paramount/WBD entity still integrating.
earnings_info: Q2 FY2026 already reported May 6, 2026: Revenue $25.17B vs $24.85B estimate (beat); EPS $1.57 vs $1.50 estimate (beat); streaming income +88% to $582M; parks revenue $9.5B (+7%). Full-year FY2026 EPS growth guided ~12%, share repurchases raised to at least $8B. Next earnings (Q3 FY2026) expected approximately August 2026.
